t: Pacifism covers a spectrum from the belief that international disputes can and should be settled peacefully to opposition to violence under any circumstance, even in defence of self and others.

Its organised form dates from 1815 and 1816, when the New York Peace Society and the London Peace Society were founded, and it drew on two strands of thought: the secular Enlightenment and the evangelical religious revival.

Mahatma Gandhi's satyagraha served as inspiration to Martin Luther King Jr. and many others in the civil rights movement, while critics from Hitler to Orwell to Jan Narveson attacked pacifism on very different grounds.
dyk: On 1 December 1948 President José Figueres Ferrer of Costa Rica abolished the Costa Rican military, and in 1949 the abolition was introduced in Article 12 of the constitution.
ev: The Quakers repudiate violence in all forms and adhere to a strictly pacifist interpretation of Christianity
The New York Peace Society is founded, and the London Peace Society follows in 1816
The London Peace Society convenes the first International Peace Congress in London
The word pacifism, coined by Émile Arnaud, is adopted at the tenth Universal Peace Congress in Glasgow
Dick Sheppard establishes the Peace Pledge Union, which totally renounces war and aggression
British activists form the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament with Bertrand Russell as its president

f.thinkers: Desiderius Erasmus, one of the most outspoken pacifists of the Renaissance; William Penn, Quaker founder of Pennsylvania; Immanuel Kant, Jean-Jacques Rousseau and Jeremy Bentham, Enlightenment writers on peace; Leo Tolstoy, who revived interest in pacifism in his late works; Mahatma Gandhi, pioneer of satyagraha; Bertha von Suttner, the first woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize; Martin Luther King Jr., who used Gandhian nonviolent resistance
f.texts: Desiderius Erasmus, The Praise of Folly (1509) and The Complaint of Peace (1517); Immanuel Kant, Thoughts on Perpetual Peace; Henry David Thoreau, Civil Disobedience; Leo Tolstoy, The Kingdom of God Is Within You; Bertha von Suttner, Die Waffen nieder! (1889); Simone Weil, The Iliad or the Poem of Force; Aldous Huxley, Ends and Means (1937)
f.ideas: rejection of war as always wrong; peaceful resolution of international disputes; institutional pacifism, the abolition of the military; nonviolent resistance and civil disobedience; conscientious objection; ahimsa, to do no harm; anarcho-pacifism; pragmatic pacifism, which holds that the costs of war are so high that better ways of settling disputes must be found
f.today: peace churches such as the Quakers, Mennonites and Church of the Brethren; Christian denominations and groups including the Catholic Worker Movement and Pax Christi; Buddhist, Jain and Hindu traditions of ahimsa; green parties that list nonviolence among their key values; constitutions that reject war, among them Italy's, Germany's and Japan's; Costa Rica, which has had no military since 1948
